title: Gladly going grey
paragraphs: Grey hair can be the beginning of the end. A silver signal that youth and beauty are fading and only old age remains. And while grey at 60 may not be surprising, many start to turn prematurely as young as 20. If we want to hide it, modern haircare products allow us to easily cover up our natural grey and preserve our youth a little longer. But these days, many people – and women in particular, are ditching the dye to show their natural colours. Why?

"Research has shown that our hair follicle production can be influenced by factors such as hormones and stress, but some people have a genetic predisposition to lose pigment or go bald more than others," says a report on the BBC website. In addition, Prof Desmond Tobin, a hair and skin pigmentation specialist at the University of Bradford in the UK, says that it is normal for people with a European background to start greying in their early 20s. Research which he participated in found that different races have different average ageing rates - with African and East-Asian backgrounds tending to whiten later.

For many men, going grey may not be a big deal. It's now seen as a sign of sophistication, says UK newspaper Metro. It uses adjectives such as rugged, unique and fashionable. But for many women, these qualities don't seem to apply. Kate Dinota, a New Yorker who started turning grey when she was seven, states that the everyday woman feels a pressure not to age. At 28 and after 14 years, she decided to stop dying her hair and let her grey hair show. And she's not alone.

Since 2008, worldwide search interest in 'grey hair' has increased dramatically, Google Trends shows. This may have been driven by celebrities such as Ariana Grande and Lady Gaga, who have both had silver locks. "People are torturing their hair to get the look," says renowned hair colourist Rita Hazan, who has worked with celebrities such as Beyoncé and Mariah Carey. Indeed, this trend was what persuaded 30-year-old Stephanie Tunchez from Texas to stop dying her natural hair two-and-a-half years ago.

But to many women, the transition is not an easy one. Indeed, Kate experienced doubt from others with her initial decision. "People were like, 'Are you sure? What about your career? You're so young!' Like that seems silly," she reports. She believes there needs to be better representation of grey-haired women of all ages. In this way it is hoped that, like many men, women will feel more confident about letting it show and will feel more comfortable going grey gracefully.

vocabulary.entry: fading /ˈfeɪdɪŋ/ adj. 逐渐消逝的；褪色的
vocabulary.example: The colour of the carpet is fading from years of use.
vocabulary.translation: 这张地毯因使用多年而褪色。

vocabulary.entry: prematurely /ˈpremətʃəli/ adv. 过早地；提前地
vocabulary.example: The flower bloomed prematurely due to the warm weather.
vocabulary.translation: 由于天气温暖，这朵花过早地绽放了。

vocabulary.entry: haircare products /ˈheəkeə ˈprɒdʌkts/ phr. 护发产品（复数）
vocabulary.example: The store sells a wide range of haircare products.
vocabulary.translation: 这家商店出售各种各样的护发产品。

vocabulary.term: cover up phr. 遮盖；掩盖
vocabulary.entry: cover up phr. 遮盖；掩盖
vocabulary.example: She tried to cover up her mistake with a lie.
vocabulary.translation: 她试图用谎言掩盖自己的错误。

vocabulary.entry: ditch the dye /dɪtʃ ðə daɪ/ phr. 放弃染发（ditch 为口语，指放弃；dye 此处为名词，指染发剂）
vocabulary.example: After years of coloring, she decided to ditch the dye.
vocabulary.translation: 染了多年头发后，她决定不再染发。

vocabulary.entry: hair follicle /heə ˈfɒlɪkl/ phr. 毛囊
vocabulary.example: Each hair grows from a tiny hair follicle in the skin.
vocabulary.translation: 每根头发都从皮肤里微小的毛囊中生长出来。

vocabulary.entry: genetic predisposition /dʒəˈnetɪk ˌpriːdɪspəˈzɪʃn/ phr. 遗传倾向；先天倾向
vocabulary.example: He has a genetic predisposition to heart disease.
vocabulary.translation: 他有心脏病的遗传倾向。

vocabulary.entry: pigment /ˈpɪɡmənt/ n. 色素；颜料
vocabulary.example: The pigment in the leaves gives them their green color.
vocabulary.translation: 叶子中的色素赋予它们绿色。

vocabulary.entry: pigmentation /ˌpɪɡmenˈteɪʃn/ n. 色素沉着；着色
vocabulary.example: The medication can cause changes in skin pigmentation.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药物可能导致皮肤色素沉着变化。

vocabulary.entry: ageing rates /ˈeɪdʒɪŋ reɪts/ phr. 衰老速度（复数）
vocabulary.example: Different factors can affect human ageing rates.
vocabulary.translation: 不同的因素会影响人类的衰老速度。

vocabulary.entry: sophistication /səˌfɪstɪˈkeɪʃn/ n. 成熟老练；精致
vocabulary.example: The hotel offers a level of sophistication rarely found in this area.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店提供的精致服务在该地区很少见。

vocabulary.entry: rugged /ˈrʌɡɪd/ adj. 粗犷的；坚毅的
vocabulary.example: The mountain landscape is rugged and beautiful.
vocabulary.translation: 这片山地景观粗犷而美丽。

vocabulary.entry: everyday woman /ˈevrideɪ ˈwʊmən/ phr. 普通女性
vocabulary.example: The brand's clothes are designed for the everyday woman.
vocabulary.translation: 这个品牌的服装是为普通女性设计的。

vocabulary.entry: dramatically /drəˈmætɪkli/ adv. 显著地；剧烈地
vocabulary.example: The situation has changed dramatically since yesterday.
vocabulary.translation: 自昨天以来，情况发生了巨大变化。

vocabulary.entry: silver locks /ˈsɪlvə lɒks/ phr. 银发；白发（locks 此处指头发）
vocabulary.example: Her silver locks were tied back in a simple bun.
vocabulary.translation: 她的银发简单地挽成一个发髻。

vocabulary.entry: torturing their hair /ˈtɔːtʃərɪŋ ðeə heə/ phr. 折腾头发（torture 此处指过度损伤）
vocabulary.example: Constant heat styling is torturing her hair.
vocabulary.translation: 频繁的热造型正在损伤她的头发。

vocabulary.entry: renowned /rɪˈnaʊnd/ adj. 著名的；有名望的
vocabulary.example: He is renowned for his work in environmental protection.
vocabulary.translation: 他因在环境保护方面的工作而闻名。

vocabulary.entry: transition /trænˈzɪʃn/ n. 过渡；转变
vocabulary.example: The transition to a new system was smooth.
vocabulary.translation: 向新系统的过渡很顺利。

vocabulary.entry: representation /ˌreprɪzenˈteɪʃn/ n. 代表性；形象展示
vocabulary.example: The film lacks representation of minority groups.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影缺乏少数群体的代表性。

vocabulary.entry: gracefully /ˈɡreɪsfəli/ adv. 优雅地；从容地
vocabulary.example: She danced gracefully across the stage.
vocabulary.translation: 她优雅地在舞台上跳舞。

vocabulary.entry: preserve /prɪˈzɜːv/ v. 保持；保存
vocabulary.example: We need to preserve these old buildings.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要保护这些古老的建筑。

vocabulary.entry: apply /əˈplaɪ/ v. 适用；应用
vocabulary.example: The new law applies to all citizens.
vocabulary.translation: 新法律适用于所有公民。
